workflow: An operation establishes an active execution context and invokes user-controlled callback code to obtain auxiliary data.
The callback re-enters the owning object and clears its active contexts, freeing a context still held by the outer operation.
The outer operation resumes without revalidating the context lifetime and reads or updates the released context.
The resulting use-after-free causes a memory-safety failure instead of safely handling the reentrant mutation.
summary: Reentrant callback frees active context before outer operation resumes
decision_reason: The bug materially matches the existing reentrant-resource-invalidation workflow: user-controlled conversion or callback code releases state that the outer operation validated and still uses afterward, leading to a use-after-free. The specific callback and profiling context are implementation-level,
